solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Seeking to influence opinion in favour of non-religious short verse

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a pagan is someone outside the main religions, here taken as non-religious

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a distich is a couplet, a pair of verse lines

explanation.surface: Someone champions secular poetry in brief form while trying to sway public opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims DISTICH, a two-line verse, to DISTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is material meant to sway public views, so the adjective describes efforts to persuade people.

clue.text: Knock a thousand off figure for survey

indicators.note: to knock something off is to remove it, so these letters are taken away from the word
together with knock, says the letters are struck out of the word

parts.note: to figure is to reckon, to calculate or suppose
K stands for a thousand, as in kilo

explanation.surface: An instruction to subtract a thousand from a total in order to produce a survey.
explanation.walkthrough: RECON is short for reconnaissance; one blog commenter noted it is chiefly American.
explanation.definitionFit: A recon, or reconnaissance, is a military survey of ground or enemy positions.

clue.text: Baked product's defunct line

parts.note: something defunct is dead and gone, in the past
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A bakery has discontinued one of its product lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastry is dough that is baked, as in pies and tarts.

clue.text: Saving lead, shoddily coated with another metal

indicators.note: shoddy work is badly put together, so these letters are assembled in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Lead has been saved but coated badly in a different metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Galvanised iron or steel has been given a protective coat of zinc.

clue.text: Feature of seaside: odd characters changing where they are and revealing all

indicators.text: odd characters changing where they are
indicators.note: the first and third letters of the seaside word trade places, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a dune is a sand hill found by the seashore

explanation.surface: Something at the beach shifts about and reveals everything, as on a naturist beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd characters changing where they are' swaps the first and third letters of DUNE, D and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone nude is wearing nothing, so everything is on show.

clue.text: Fast mover picked up risqué tips from dating network insider

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means the letters are read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: racy means slightly indecent, risqué

indicators.note: the tips of words are their first letters, taken from each of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone overhears saucy advice from a person inside a dating agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' looks like a homophone signal but means lifting the letters upwards in this down entry: RACY + DNI reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: An IndyCar is a fast open-wheel racing car of the American series, a speedy machine.

clue.text: Work on structure increasing strength in eyes

indicators.note: the strengthening word sits within the word for eyes

parts.note: private eyes are detectives, 'tecs for short
a tonic is something that builds up strength

explanation.surface: Exercises to build up the strength of the eyes, as in a vision-training structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Tectonics is the study or science of structure, whether in building or in the earth's crust.

clue.text: Secretive, devious dark agenda encircles head of government, close to summit

indicators.note: in a down clue the summit is the top, so this piece is placed first

parts.note: CL is the street-name abbreviation for Close

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the other piece
devious means winding or crooked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the phrase as printed gives only ten letters; the setter's anagram needs an O as well, which no word of the clue supplies

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A government leader caught up in some shady, scheming plot near the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devious' rearranges DARK AGENDA round G ('head of government'), with CL ('close') put first by 'to summit'; but those letters give only thirteen, so the setter's fodder lacks the O the answer needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloak-and-dagger describes intrigue and espionage, activity carried out in secret.

clue.text: Add sauce and try again with reduced seasoning — this may be the last chance to get it right!

definitions.text: this may be the last chance to get it right!

parts.note: to dress a salad or dish is to add sauce to it
to rehear a case is to try it again in court

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: salt is a seasoning

explanation.surface: Cooking advice: pour on sauce and taste again with less salt before serving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try again' is legal, a court trying a case again; 'reduced' drops the last letter of SALT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress rehearsal is the final full run-through before a performance opens.

clue.text: Firm's rank on ice

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: rocks is slang for ice, as in a drink served on the rocks; also slang for diamonds
olid is a rare word for foul-smelling, rank

explanation.surface: A company's foul-smelling stock is being kept chilled on ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock-solid means utterly firm and dependable, unshakable.

clue.text: Glimpse ground zero

parts.note: deck is slang for the ground or floor, as in hitting the deck
O looks like the figure zero

explanation.surface: Catching sight of Ground Zero, the site in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: DECKO, from Hindi, is British slang for a look and is more often spelt DEKKO.
explanation.definitionFit: A decko is a quick look, a peek in British slang.

clue.text: Belted out melody after knocking back drink

indicators.note: the backwards tune comes after the singing word

parts.note: to belt out a song is to sing it loudly

indicators.note: knocking back here means turning the letters backwards

parts.note: an air is a tune, a melody

explanation.surface: Someone sang loudly after downing a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking back' looks like part of the drinking scene, but it reverses AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine and fruit, a drink.

clue.text: Old chap's suppressing hint of laughter, as shown by face?

indicators.note: suppressing means holding something down within, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: cock is old slang for a chap, as in 'old cock'

indicators.note: a hint of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An old fellow trying not to laugh, which shows on his face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face' is a clock face, not a human one, which the question mark admits.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying a time is so many o'clock means as read on a clock's face.

clue.text: Run railway to increase efficiency

parts.note: a run is a small stream, as in American usage
a railway line

explanation.surface: Operating a railway in order to make it more efficient.
explanation.definitionFit: To streamline is to make a process simpler and more efficient.

clue.text: Moroccan bar-owner showing strain

definitions.meaning: ... Blaine owns a bar in Casablanca in the film
to wrench or sprain a joint

explanation.definitionFit: Humphrey Bogart's character runs Rick's Café in Casablanca; a rick is also a sprain or wrench.

clue.text: Popular chemical firm formerly controlled by family doctor

indicators.note: being controlled by something is being held within it

parts.note: a clan is an extended family
in means fashionable, popular
ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a major British chemical company, now gone

explanation.surface: A family doctor's shares in a once-popular chemical company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'family doctor' looks like the definition, but 'family' supplies CLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinician is a medical practitioner who treats patients directly.

clue.text: One obeying order to surround agents with tank

indicators.note: the tank word goes round the agents

parts.note: a cistern is a water tank
the CIA is the American intelligence agency, a body of agents

explanation.surface: An instruction to encircle spies with an armoured vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' is a monastic order, not a command; 'tank' is a water tank, not a military one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cistercian is a monk or nun of the Cistercian religious order.

clue.text: Heeding the tremors, climbed further

indicators.note: tremors shake things up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Mindful of the earth tremors, climbers went higher up.
explanation.definitionFit: Heightened means raised higher, so the level has risen further.

clue.text: Was Observer supporting journalist's cutting article?

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, a hack's being one's
saw means observed, was an observer

explanation.surface: A query about whether the Observer newspaper backed a reporter's biting article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observer' looks like the newspaper but is someone watching.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a saw for cutting metal, a tool or article used for cutting.

clue.text: Employed New York Times boss, say

parts.note: New York is in the US, an example signalled by say
the boss of a newspaper such as The Times is the editor, ED

explanation.surface: A newspaper chief at the New York Times has been hired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks both pieces as examples: New York stands for the US, a Times boss for an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Used means employed, put to use.

clue.text: Chanel applied to produce stage in metamorphosis

parts.note: Coco Chanel was the French fashion designer
something applied is put on

explanation.surface: Chanel cosmetics applied to bring about a transformation.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocoon is the silk case a caterpillar spins before turning into a moth.

clue.text: Each pasty's excellent to eat

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: ace means excellent
a pasty is a pastry case with filling, a pie

explanation.surface: Every pasty here is delicious to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece means for each one, as in a pound apiece.

clue.text: Low bit of chain making fast

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
a chain is made of links or rings

explanation.surface: A low link in a chain holds things fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooring a boat is securing it, tying it fast to a buoy or quay.

clue.text: Clerics don't miss me?

parts.note: said by a woman who prefers the title Ms to Miss, and so may say she is a Ms

explanation.surface: A cleric asks plaintively whether anyone will miss them.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as I'M A MS, the answer is a woman insisting on Ms, not Miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Imams are Muslim leaders of prayer in a mosque, religious clerics.

clue.text: Resort lacking bar?

parts.note: O stands for nothing, zero, the state of lacking
to bar is to ban, and a ban is a bar

explanation.surface: A seaside resort with no pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as O BAN, the answer is 'no ban', no bar. OBAN is a seaside town in western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a Scottish holiday resort and ferry port on the west coast.

clue.text: Space station bearing first citizen of neutral country

indicators.note: the compass bearing goes first, before the station

parts.note: SW, south-west, is a compass bearing
the ISS is the International Space Station

explanation.surface: A space station heads off, carrying the first citizen of a neutral nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Switzerland is famously neutral, and a Swiss is a person from there.

clue.text: Artwork made from a clog, creatively coated in cheese

indicators.note: the reworked letters sit inside the cheese, coated by it

parts.note: brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: creatively means made anew, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A sculpture made from a wooden shoe and covered in cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made from' looks like part of the definition's phrasing but only links it; BRIE is a soft French cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Bricolage is art built from whatever materials are to hand.

clue.text: Was desperate to reach point, interrupted by waffle and verbosity

indicators.note: the headland is reached at the end, so it comes last
the waffle word breaks into the yearning word

parts.note: longed means yearned, was desperate
wind is empty talk, waffle
a ness is a headland or promontory, a point

explanation.surface: A speaker desperate to get to the point keeps being interrupted by waffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-windedness is talking or writing at tedious length, wordiness.
